pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome | Top Nursery School | Broadhurst School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Broadhurst School – A Leading Nursery School in London
Welcome to Broadhurst School, a place where curiosity, creativity, and excellence come to life. I am truly honoured to lead such a warm and aspirational nursery, steeped in history and a deep commitment to early childhood education.
For generations, Broadhurst has been at the forefront of nurturing young learners, providing a strong foundation as they embark on their educational journey. Rooted in tradition yet always forward-thinking, we provide a rich, stimulating environment where young minds thrive.
Our carefully designed early years curriculum reflects the latest educational insights, ensuring that every child develops the knowledge, skills, and confidence to navigate an ever-evolving world. Through engaging, hands-on experiences, both indoors and outdoors, every child has the opportunity to explore, experiment, and grow in ways that are meaningful to them.
At Broadhurst, I see learning as something deeply personal and unique to each child. Our exceptional staff craft imaginative and inspiring experiences that spark curiosity, foster independence, and instil a lifelong love of learning. By the time children leave us, I want them to be not only well-prepared for the next stage of their education but also brimming with self-assurance, joy, and a sense of wonder.
A nurturing and secure environment is at the heart of everything we do. Children thrive when they feel valued, supported, and encouraged to take on new challenges. With high expectations and an unwavering commitment to excellence, I am proud to continue Broadhurst’s tradition of offering an education that is both enriching and full of joy.
I look forward to welcoming you and your child into our vibrant school community.
Ms Paula Flindall Headteacher, Broadhurst School

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us | Private School London | Broadhurst School
pageCache.text:
Widely regarded as one of London’s leading nursery schools, Broadhurst School has been inspiring young learners since 1958. Situated in West Hampstead, at the heart of a community spanning Hampstead, St John’s Wood, Queen’s Park and beyond, we offer an exceptional early years education through a carefully designed curriculum that balances academic ambition with the joy of learning through play.
Small class sizes allow teachers and teaching assistants to build strong, trusting relationships with every child, supporting their development and wellbeing. Children are encouraged to question, explore, problem-solve and embrace new challenges with confidence – developing the skills, curiosity and resilience to thrive at school and in life beyond it.
We have a strong record in preparing children for the 4+ assessment process and successful entry into leading London pre-preparatory and preparatory schools. Our focus, however, is always on the whole child. We aim to foster a genuine love of learning, so that every child feels proud of how far they have come and excited to return each day ready for new experiences.
Working closely with families and future schools, we ensure each child leaves Broadhurst well-prepared, self-assured and ready for the next stage of their educational journey.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parent Partnerships | Private Nursery | Broadhurst School
pageCache.text:
We believe that a strong partnership between home and school is central to every child’s happiness and progress. We work closely with families to create an open, welcoming community where parents feel genuinely involved in school life.
Staying Connected
Regular communication is at the heart of our relationship with families. Parents are welcome to speak with their child’s teacher at the beginning or end of the day, and more formal Parent-Teacher Meetings are held in the autumn and spring terms, giving families dedicated time to discuss their child’s development.
Each term, we also hold Parent and Child Mornings, which is a wonderful opportunity for families to come into school and share in their child’s learning firsthand.
Getting Involved
We warmly encourage parents to play an active role in school life. Whether it is accompanying children on a school trip, reading a favourite story to the class, or sharing knowledge of a cultural tradition, parental contributions enrich the experience of every child at Broadhurst.
Parents are also welcome to talk to the class about their profession – children are particularly delighted when visitors arrive in uniform. If you have a skill or area of expertise you would like to offer, such as gardening or cooking, we would love to hear from you.
Cultural Celebrations and Community Events
Throughout the year, Broadhurst marks a wide range of cultural and international celebrations, from Diwali and Easter to St Valentine’s Day and Mother’s Day. Parents are always encouraged to come in and share their own traditions, whether through stories, music or dress, helping children develop an appreciation of the diverse world around them.
Our whole-school community events bring families together across the year and include Children in Need, World Book Day, Sports Day and our much-loved annual Summer Garden Party.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care and Wellbeing | Broadhurst School
pageCache.text:
At Broadhurst School, we believe children flourish when they feel safe, valued, respected and emotionally secure. Nurturing wellbeing is at the heart of everything we do, creating an environment where children develop the confidence, resilience and self-belief to thrive both academically and personally.
Our warm and caring staff build strong relationships with every child, ensuring they feel known, heard and supported. We place great importance on helping children understand and express their emotions, modelling and developing emotional language from an early age so that children can communicate their feelings with confidence and empathy.
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Through our enriched PSED curriculum, children learn strategies for emotional regulation, positive relationships and self-awareness. Mindfulness, yoga, creative movement and drama are woven throughout school life, helping children develop calm minds, healthy bodies and a positive sense of self. Calm and reflective spaces within classrooms provide opportunities for children to regulate emotions, practise self-management and return to learning feeling ready and supported.
We promote a restorative approach to behaviour and relationships, helping children understand the impact of their actions, resolve disagreements positively and develop empathy for others. Through restorative conversations and guided reflection, children learn valuable lifelong skills in communication, responsibility and problem-solving.
Finding Their Voice
Children are encouraged to develop confidence through a wide range of opportunities to perform, present and share their achievements. Whether participating in drama productions, musical performances, Show and Tell sessions or classroom discussions, children are supported to find and use their voice.
Active and Responsible Citizens
We believe in empowering children to become active and responsible members of their community. From an early age, children learn about fairness, respect, democracy and inclusion. They are given meaningful opportunities to make choices, vote on aspects of school life and contribute their ideas, helping them understand that their opinions matter and that everyone has a voice.
Above all, we strive to create a culture where every child feels happy, secure and valued as the unique individual they are. By supporting wellbeing alongside academic development, we help children build the confidence, resilience and emotional intelligence that will serve them throughout their education and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Heritage | Private Nursery London | Broadhurst School
pageCache.text:
A Family-Run Nursery School Since 1958
Broadhurst School was founded in 1958 by Mrs Mary Berkery with a clear ambition: to raise the standard of early years education through a rigorous, accelerated programme tailored to the curiosity and potential of very young children. Drawing on her Montessori training, Mrs Berkery created a welcoming and calm environment especially designed for children to make independent enquiry and learn through practical and specialised methods.
Almost seven decades on, the school remains in the family, with Mrs Berkery’s son, Mr Brian Berkery, as proprietor. He carries forward her legacy with the same commitment to quality and individual attention. In a world where school ownership frequently changes hands, this continuity is genuinely rare and deeply valued by the families who choose us.
Just as Mrs Berkery believed from the very beginning, children learn best through play, exploration and discovery, and that belief remains at the heart of everything we do at Broadhurst today. Our individual daily sessions with each child sit alongside a rich programme of playful, creative experiences, so that every pupil leaves us confident, curious and truly prepared for the next chapter.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum | Top Nursery London | Broadhurst School
pageCache.text:
At Broadhurst School, we believe the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) is a vital and formative part of every child’s learning journey. Our play-based curriculum is carefully designed to inspire curiosity, creativity and confidence, while providing children with the strong academic foundations they need to flourish.
We recognise that young children learn best through meaningful experiences, active exploration and warm, secure relationships. Play lies at the heart of our approach and is fundamental to children’s cognitive, social, emotional and physical development. Through a carefully planned balance of adult-led teaching, child-initiated learning and purposeful play, children develop independence, resilience, communication skills and a genuine love of learning.
Small class sizes allow teachers and teaching assistants to build strong relationships with every child, ensuring learning is responsive to individual interests, strengths and developmental needs. We place great importance on nurturing the whole child, supporting wellbeing, emotional security and self-esteem alongside academic progress.
Structured and Accelerated Learning
Our rich curriculum supports all seven areas of the EYFS framework, including:
As children prepare for competitive 4+ assessments, we offer an accelerated programme that develops early literacy, mathematical understanding, reasoning, language and interview confidence in a nurturing and age-appropriate way.
Alongside academic readiness, we place great importance on developing the personal qualities and characteristics that enable children to thrive both within the assessment process and beyond. We encourage children to be curious, articulate and willing to have a go, developing confidence in themselves as learners. These characteristics are embedded within everyday life at Broadhurst School and are nurtured through meaningful relationships, collaborative play, rich conversation and carefully planned learning experiences.
We believe that happy, confident and well-rounded children are best placed to succeed, and this is consistently reflected in the children we see flourishing throughout our school community.

Curriculum Enrichment
We enrich children’s experiences through specialist teaching across a wide range of subjects, including Music, Drama, Science, Cultural Studies, Yoga, Mindfulness and Physical Education. These experiences broaden children’s understanding of the world, encourage creativity and support the development of confident, well-rounded learners.
Children also benefit from educational visits and hands-on experiences linked closely to their classroom learning. We believe young children learn best through real-life, concrete experiences that bring topics to life, deepen understanding and inspire curiosity. Trips, visitors and practical experiences help children make meaningful connections with the world around them, enriching their language, imagination and understanding.
Broadhurst School has a long-established record of success with destination schools, and strong partnerships with receiving schools support each child’s smooth transition to the next stage of education. Above all, we strive to create an environment where children feel happy, valued and excited to learn – developing the confidence, curiosity, resilience and strong foundations that will serve them throughout their education and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Broadhurst Sports Day Brings Smiles, Team Spirit and Plenty of Joy - Broadhurst School
pageCache.text:
There was no shortage of excitement at our recent Sports Day as the children took to the field for a morning of movement, encouragement and fun. While there may not have been Olympic records to break, there were plenty of proud moments as the children enthusiastically joined in with the activities and cheered on their friends.
Our youngest pupils enjoyed taking part in simple running races, while the older children tackled a series of obstacle-course challenges that tested their coordination and determination. At this age, Sports Day is not about winning medals or finishing first; it is about building confidence, developing physical skills and, most importantly, enjoying being active together. It was wonderful to see every child taking part with enthusiasm and a smile.
The excitement continued with the ever-popular parents’ and teachers’ races. The mums, dads and staff all rose to the challenge, much to the delight of the children, who thoroughly enjoyed seeing the grown-ups embrace their competitive side. The cheering from the sidelines was every bit as enthusiastic as the races themselves.
The event concluded with a special performance from the children’s favourite entertainer, Mr Shakabula. His unique blend of magic, music and comedy had the children captivated from start to finish, providing the perfect finale to a memorable day.
Sports Day was a wonderful celebration of friendship, participation and community spirit at Broadhurst School. We are incredibly proud of all our children for embracing every challenge with enthusiasm, confidence and a willingness to give their very best.

Application Process
Children typically join Broadhurst School in September following their second birthday. An early January start is available for children who turn two between September and January of the same academic year.
How to Apply
1. Enquire online
Complete the enquiry form to arrange a school visit or register your interest in a place.
2. Visit the school
The Registrar will contact you to arrange a convenient date for a tour and a meeting with the Headteacher. Visits are arranged in small groups of two or three families, allowing for a more personalised experience and the opportunity to ask questions.
3. Secure your place
Following your visit, parents will be offered a place and asked to complete an Acceptance Form and pay both a registration fee and an Acceptance Deposit to confirm enrolment.
We also occasionally host Stay and Play sessions, where prospective families are welcome to join in with activities, meet the staff, and get to know other parents.
Places are allocated on a first come, first served basis, in order of application. A place is not confirmed until a visit has taken place and an Acceptance Deposit has been received.
Fees and Payment
One year before your child’s proposed start date, parents are asked to pay a non-returnable advance of £500 against the first term’s fees. The remaining balance is due eight months before the start date.
From the second term onwards, fees are payable on the first day of each new term.
